findings.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/GroupAdapter.java:275 — [P1/C75] `return model == null ? null : model.getSubGroupsCount();` changes `null` from “subgroup count was not requested” to “the group disappeared during lookup,” so a count-enabled group-list response serializes a deleted cached group with an indistinguishable absent count instead of enforcing a consistent deleted-entity policy.

model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/GroupAdapter.java:256 — [P2/C75][advisory] `return modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(search, firstResult, maxResults);` alongside the bespoke null branch at line 275 scatters deleted-delegate policy across accessors, so the next concurrent-deletion path through an unpatched accessor still dereferences null; although the current endpoint exercises the count accessor, the same adapter exposes every accessor, and central lifecycle resolution deletes the repeated branches and per-accessor update points.

docs/tasks/task-001.md:1 — P2/C100: `# Task: Fix concurrent group access to prevent NullPointerException` defines neither the affected access path nor the required deleted-group result, so the change can return `null` without any acceptance criterion establishing that callers receive the contractually correct response instead of merely avoiding one exception.

model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/GroupAdapter.java:256 — P1/C75: `return modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(search, firstResult, maxResults);` still dereferences the same nullable supplier during concurrent deletion, so paginated subgroup access continues to throw NullPointerException even though the task claims concurrent group access is fixed.

model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/GroupAdapter.java:275 — Advisory P2/C75: `return model == null ? null : model.getSubGroupsCount();` silently produces a successful group representation with `subGroupCount=null` when deletion wins the lookup race, so clients requesting subgroup counts receive partial data indistinguishable from a response where counts were not requested; although a weakly consistent listing can include a concurrently deleted group, that does not make an explicitly requested numeric field optional without an omission marker.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/GroupUtils.java:102 — P3 C100: deleting `private static boolean groupMatchesSearchOrIsPathElement(GroupModel group, String search)` is unrelated to concurrent group access and couples search-helper cleanup to the NPE hotfix, so reverting the hotfix necessarily resurrects unrelated dead code.

tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:139 — [P1/C100] `new Thread(() -> { ... }).start();` starts the reader without a start barrier, so the deletion loop can finish and set `deletedAll` before the reader executes, allowing this regression test to pass without exercising concurrent group access.

tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:155 — [P1/C100] `deletedAll.set(true);` is followed immediately by `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty());` without joining the reader thread, so an in-flight read can throw and append after the assertion, allowing the exact NullPointerException regression to pass unnoticed.

goldens.comment: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() violates the GroupModel contract (Javadoc says it never returns null) and may lead to NPEs in callers that expect a non-null count.
The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.
